To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) multiple key hashing is a good approach for a file with many keys and many records, and b) a combination of inversion and hashing is the best approach for a file of moderate size with few keys per record.
(1) the cost of page accessing is the dominant cost in a paged environment and (2) the best way of organizing a file is to invert the keys that are accessed most frequently and hash the rest.
a combined method of inversion and multiple key hashing can be used to achieve a factor of 3 improvement in file access costs over a simple inversion method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of data structures which are suitable for use in paged memory environments and which minimize the number of page faults incurred in accessing data.
the design of data organizations for files which must be accessed frequently in a paged environment.
the organization of files which are to be maintained in a paged secondary memory.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the cost of page accessing in paged memory is so high that it can easily dominate other file organization costs, and therefore, file organizations must be designed with page accesses in mind.
, in a memory environment, the cost of accessing a page is a key factor in determining the best data organization for a given set of retrieval characteristics.
the cost of page access is a major factor that must be considered when choosing a file organization.
